" Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. I bought this two-pack because I wanted to upgrade from a basic electric toothbrush, and I’m really pleased with it so far. The difference is noticeable straight away. My teeth feel much cleaner after brushing, and the iO2 is surprisingly quiet compared with other electric toothbrushes I’ve used. I really like having the pressure sensor because it’s easy to accidentally brush too hard, and the different intensity settings mean I can adjust it depending on how my teeth and gums feel. The handles are comfortable to hold and the battery life has been good, so I’m not constantly having to charge them. Getting two handles, two brush heads and the travel cases makes this feel like a much better deal than buying a single toothbrush. The black and forest green colours also look much better than the usual plain toothbrushes. The only thing I’d mention is to rinse the brush and handle properly after use, as toothpaste can build up around the head and smaller areas. Overall, I’m very happy with the purchase. It feels like a genuine upgrade from a standard electric toothbrush and I’d definitely recommend the iO2, particularly if you can get the two-pack at a good price. Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 12 April 2025 Colour Name: Black Verified Purchase Brief content visible, double tap to read full content. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. It is nice to just buy normal nail polish without gel or other things now. I like black and I just wanted some cheap varnish to cover my nails. I have issues with my nails, they snap or break off very easily since a teen. The actual varnish is like a mini version when it arrived, the brush does have a lot on it, so goes quite wide over the finger. The varnish is jet black, but not thick. The liquid is just that liquid, so be careful. I applied one coat which does cover well, but very matte like. So to get a bit of shine will need a top coat, or another coat of the black. Although I have two coats on and a decent enough shine, ensure it is dried completely, otherwise it will come off. The most ridiculous thing I’ve heard is the 60 seconds of drying. Please do not count on this as yes I timed it. I picked one nail and timed 60 seconds, it was tacky dry and when I touched the top of my nails, there was an imprint of my finger, ie finger print left behind. So yes after 60 seconds my nails were tacky but not completely dry. After two coats I left 10 minutes. Best to leave as long as you can. So many times I have had to go over the nail. Feels nice and smooth when on. Had mine on for a few days now with no chips. If you happen to catch your polished nail on the side board for example, it will scratch off. All in all this is fine for a cheap nail polish, but do not be fooled by the 60 seconds. I have tried this previously and thought I would give it another try, but I won’t bother again.. there are better out there, this is cheap and cheerful. Product description Product Description Just For Men Moustache & Beard M45 – Dark Brown Black Dye is a specially formulated solution designed to provide you with natural-looking color while eliminating gray from your facial hair. This Dark Brown Black (M45) shade offers a deep, rich color that blends seamlessly with your natural hair, giving your beard or mustache a fuller, thicker appearance. Whether you're looking to cover gray hair or enhance your natural color, Just For Men M45 is the perfect solution for a well-groomed, youthful look. The unique formula is designed to work quickly, with results in just 5 minutes , giving you the flexibility and convenience to incorporate this into your daily grooming routine. The no-mix application means there’s no hassle, and the product is ready to use right out of the box. An easy-to-use applicator brush is included to ensure precise application, allowing you to target specific areas for uniform, mess-free coverage. In addition to providing excellent gray coverage, Just For Men M45 also promotes a thicker, fuller appearance. This helps you achieve a beard or mustache that looks more robust and healthy, enhancing your natural features and boosting your confidence. The formula is ammonia-free , gentle on your skin, and enriched with conditioning agents to ensure your facial hair stays soft and smooth, without the dryness or damage associated with other dyes. Just For Men M45 is dermatologist-tested and safe for all skin types, offering a long-lasting solution that resists fading through multiple washes. Achieve your desired look without worrying about touch-ups, and enjoy a more youthful, refreshed appearance every day. Whether you're aiming to cover gray, enhance your natural color, or simply achieve a thicker and more defined beard or mustache, Just For Men M45 – Dark Brown Black Dye is your go-to choice for reliable, natural-looking results. Patch Test: Conduct a patch test 48 hours before each application to check for allergic reactions. Apply a small amount of the mixed dye behind your ear or on the inner bend of your elbow. If irritation or redness occurs, discontinue use immediately. 2. Avoid Contact: Take precautions to avoid getting the dye mixture into your eyes. If contact occurs, rinse thoroughly with water and seek medical attention if irritation persists. 3. External Use Only: This product is for external use on eyebrows only. Do not use on eyelashes or other areas of the body. Keep out of reach of children. 4. Chemical Sensitivity: If you have sensitive skin or have experienced adverse reactions to hair dye in the past, consult a dermatologist before using this product. 5. Storage: Store the dye kit in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight and heat sources. Ensure the product is tightly sealed when not in use. 6. Use as Directed: Follow the application instructions provided with the kit carefully. Do not exceed the recommended development time, as this may result in skin irritation or over-darkening of the eyebrows. 7. Allergic Reactions: If you experience any discomfort, burning, or itching during or after application, remove the dye immediately and rinse with lukewarm water. Seek medical advice if symptoms persist. By using this product, you agree to assume all risks associated with its use. Discontinue use if any adverse reactions occur and consult a healthcare professional if necessary. Product description Product Description An interdental brush is the most efficient way to remove plaque between the teeth in a user-friendly way. It's designed to clean the gaps where a regular toothbrush is unable to reach. By only using a toothbrush you clean 60% of your teeth, but by adding an interdental brush to your oral care routine, you will clean up to 100% of your teeth. The TePe Interdental Brush Original Yellow has a larger brush size (ISO size 4) and have a thicker, bendable wire. The interdental brush, which is available in 9 different sizes, can be used for cleaning between teeth, implants, bridges, and crowns. Use daily to keep teeth and gums healthy and fresh. For the last few years, my washing machine had been giving off the most horrendous smell after each wash, which I can only describe as an ungodly mix of sewage, garlic, and egg. It was absolutely disgusting, and the smell would spread throughout the house. I tried every solution I could think of, including bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, hot cycles, and even other chemical cleaners, but nothing worked. I cleaned every part of the machine, replaced the pipes, scrubbed the detergent drawer, cleaned the drip tray, and ran hot washes, but the smell just wouldn't go away. I was at my wit's end, especially with guests coming to stay, and I couldn’t bear the thought of them waking up to that awful odour. So, I scoured Amazon one last time and came across this Dr. Beckmann Service-it Deep Clean Washing Machine Cleaner. Its bold claims of removing 99.99% of bacteria, fungi, and viruses, as well as eliminating bad odours, seemed too good to be true, so I had to try it! All I can say is wow! Using it couldn’t be easier. Just empty the whole 250g box into the drum, no measuring required, and set your machine to run at a minimum of 60°C for at least an hour. I opted for a 90°C wash, which lasts for 2 hours on my machine, for extra thoroughness. After just one wash, the disgusting smell that had plagued my home for years was completely gone, and three weeks later, it still hasn’t returned. I’m absolutely amazed at how effective this product is. It left no mess, no residue, and it feels like I have a brand-new washing machine. For the price, it’s unbeatable. I paid £2.90 for the 250g pack, which is enough for one full clean, and I’ve seen the price drop lower. Given how effective it is, that’s an absolute bargain! I’ve already ordered a few more packs to use regularly, as it’s recommended to use every 1-2 months to keep your machine in top shape. The cleaner is supposed to leave a lemon fresh scent, though I didn’t really notice that. But honestly, the fact that my machine no longer smells at all is a win for me. Now all I can smell is my laundry detergent, and that’s good enough! I’ve tried a lot of other products, including well-known brands like Dettol, but none of them were able to tackle the odour like this. It also worked wonders on the limescale build-up in my 20-year-old machine, leaving the drum and seals sparkling clean. This cleaner is suitable for both front-loading and top-loading machines, and it’s great for prolonging the life of your appliance by preventing limescale and dirt build-up. If you’ve been dealing with an awful odour in your washing machine like I was, I can’t recommend this product enough. I wish I had found it sooner. It would have saved me so much frustration. I’ll definitely be using it regularly from now on, and I’m excited to try more from the Dr. Beckmann range. If you’re looking for a product that truly works and is great value for money, this is it! Followed the instructions but instead of lifting the solution as described, we used the VAX with water only to rinse it then to lift the residue. It has a soft chemical but very pleasant odour to it which is a great feature as the pungent about from the rotten potatoes has also gone. The carpet does not appear to have been affected negatively in any way and so far, we cannot see any noticeable discolouration which is always a bonus. Ignore the expensive options, try this - if it can lift three week old potato goo smoked into a silver carpet I bet it can handle most things! LOW BATTERY ALERT: A flashing amber '!' and an audible chirp will alert you when the batteries need replacing. CRESCENDO TEST: This feature helps to protect your hearing by allowing you to choose the volume level of the test alarm. In the event of the CO alarm sounding, follow these 3 steps: VENTILATE : Keep calm; open doors and windows to ventilate your home. Stop using fuel-burning appliances and turn them off. EVACUATE : Evacuate the property immediately. RING FOR HELP: If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. Do not use appliances until they have been checked by an expert. Get medical help for anyone suffering the effects of CO poisoning. What are the symptoms of CO poisoning? Symptoms of CO poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, seizures, chest pain, disorientation, and loss of consciousness. Who should I call in the event of a CO leak? If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. What are the sources of CO? The common sources of Carbon Monoxide (CO) are cookers, fires, boilers, oil and gas boilers, portable generators, oil or solid fuel cookers, gas or paraffin heaters, barbecues (BBQs), clogged chimneys, wood or gas fireplaces, cigarette smoke or any fossil fuel‑burning appliances. The biggest strength is the absorbency and odour control. The granules act like a sponge, locking in moisture quickly before smells develop, which really helps keep the litter tray fresh between full changes. It also uses a mineral protection system that reduces ammonia odours, so it doesn’t get unpleasant too quickly. Another thing I like is that it’s unscented and made from natural materials (quartz and limestone), so there’s no artificial fragrance masking smells just straightforward hygiene. That makes it a good choice if your cat is sensitive or picky about scented litter. The low dust is also noticeable when pouring it into the tray, which is a bonus for both you and your cat. And the white colour makes it easier to spot when it needs changing. A few downsides: It’s non-clumping, so you can’t just scoop out urine you’ll need to change the whole tray more regularly The granules can track a bit outside the tray Large 20L bag can be a bit heavy to handle Overall, it’s a dependable, hygienic litter that does exactly what it promises without overcomplicating things. Verdict: A great everyday cat litter with strong odour control and natural ingredients—ideal if you prefer non-clumping, low-maintenance options. I genuinely recommend it to everyone! This is, without exaggeration, my absolute favourite mascara of all time. I've tried more expensive mascaras in the past, and honestly, none of them have even come close to how good this one is. For the price, I genuinely think this is one of the best mascaras you can buy. I always get it in the black shade, and I have absolutely no complaints whatsoever. Every single time I wear this mascara, I get compliments on my eyelashes. I've genuinely had people ask me what mascara I'm wearing, and some people have even thought I was wearing fake lashes because of how long and full they look! The length it gives my lashes is honestly amazing, but it's not just length either. It gives them really good volume and makes them look so much more dramatic. One of my favourite things about it is the lift it gives as well. People have asked me if I've curled my eyelashes, but I literally never curl them. I don't even feel like I need to when I'm wearing this mascara because it makes them look so lifted and curled on its own. It also layers really well, which I love. You don't need to spend ages applying loads and loads of coats either. Just a couple of layers and the difference is honestly amazing. It's quick and easy to apply, but you can also build it up if you want a more dramatic look without it feeling like you have to fight with the mascara to get the effect you want. Another massive plus for me is how easily it comes off at the end of the day. This one is completely different. I usually just wash my face in the shower, and it comes off really easily with water, which I personally find so convenient. It also lasts me really well. I would say one tube lasts me around two months, possibly even a little longer depending on how often I'm wearing it, which makes it even better value for money. I've bought much more expensive mascaras before thinking they must surely be better, but I've honestly been disappointed so many times. This mascara proves that you really don't need to spend loads of money to get amazing results. I genuinely recommend this to everyone who asks me what mascara they should buy. These gloves are excellent! I originally bought them for 3D printing, as many companies recommend nitrile gloves when handling 3D-printed resins. When working with resin, especially liquid resins and Isopropanol alcohol, it is crucial to have reliable gloves, and these do the job perfectly. The fit is incredible; they feel like a second skin, making tasks like removing supports from 3D prints a breeze. The textured surface ensures a firm grip, even when handling slippery or delicate objects, while their stretchability enhances dexterity and control. Whether you are working with intricate parts or handling liquids, these gloves give you a secure and confident hold. While I initially expected them to be thinner due to the price, I was pleasantly surprised. They are thick enough to offer serious protection but not so thick that they limit movement. I have used them with both liquid resin and Isopropanol, and they have never torn, punctured, or shown any signs of degradation during use. Their puncture resistance is a significant advantage, especially when working with sharp tools or rough materials. Although I originally bought these for single use, they are definitely strong enough to be reused multiple times, depending on the task. If I am just cleaning or doing light work, I wash them with soap while still wearing them, turn them inside out to dry, and they are good to go for another use. This makes them even more cost-effective. We always keep a box of these gloves in the house, as they are perfect for everything from scrubbing the oven and cleaning the toilet to handling my cat's litter tray, food preparation, first aid, or any task that requires thorough hand protection. I recently started using them when cleaning my water filtration system to avoid contamination, and they work perfectly for that as well. The fit is excellent too. I have large hands, and the large size fits me well, though they are slightly tight, which I prefer because it gives me more control over what I am doing. I would estimate they are about a size 9, which is perfect for my hands. They are also latex-free, so they do not irritate my skin at all, which is a huge bonus for anyone with allergies or sensitivities. Another great feature is how easy they are to put on and take off. Even after wearing them for an extended period, they do not stick to my skin, and there is no hassle when it comes to removing them. I have had gloves in the past that became difficult to remove after long use, but not these. For £5.75 for a box of 100 large gloves, the value for money is outstanding. The quality is on par with, if not better than, more expensive brands I have tried. The packaging was sturdy and secure, and you can actually remove one glove at a time from the box without pulling out a clump. These gloves are definitely some of the best I have used. If you are looking for reliable, durable, and versatile nitrile gloves for any task, whether it is 3D printing, cleaning, food prep, or messy jobs around the house, I cannot recommend these highly enough! Brand Gritin Colour Silver Material Aluminium, Plastic Style Modern Light fixture form Wall About this item Upgraded Premium Functionality: Built-in 84 super bright LEDs, the Gritin under cabinet light is crafted with aluminum alloy and durable ABS plastic for ultimate strength and style. Setting the under cabinet lights on motion sensor mode, it features a 120° wide sensing angle and a 3M/10FT detection distance, automatically turning off after 20 seconds of no motion detected, ensuring you never fumble for switches. Adjustable 3-Color Temperature & 5-Brightness: Equipped with 3 color temperatures: warm (3000K) for cozy spaces, cool (6000K) for task lighting, and balanced mixed (4500K) for versatile use. Easily switch between modes with a one-touch temperature button and creates a sense of atmosphere. Setting the brightness levels from 10%, 25%,50%, 75%, to 100%, or A long press activates stepless dimming, meets different lighting needs. It features a brightness/color temperature memory function. 4 Lighting Modes: The motion sensor lights support four modes to meet the needs of different occasions: OFF Mode, Night Sensing Mode (motion-activated in darkness), Daytime Sensing Mode (motion-activated at any time whether the environment is dark or not) and Always on Mode (constant light). The auto-sensing functionality ensures optimal lighting utilization, making it ideal for kitchens, closets, cupboards, pantries, stairs, basement and other spaces needing reliable lighting. USB-C Rechargeable & Long-lasting: Built-in 1800mAh high-capacity battery, it offers up to 8 hrs in high brightness mode and lasts 7-45 days in sensor mode. It can be easily recharged by the type-C cable, no need to charge frenquently. It's the perfect choice for upgrading your home lighting! (2 USB-C cables included). Ease of Installation & Wide Usage: With built-in strong magnets, these cabinet lights can be easily installed on iron surfaces. For non-metallic surface, you can use the included adhesive iron plates to stick on anywhere you want, which means that it's easy to take off and put back on when it needs a charge. I understand that the longevity of the battery will depend on it use and also cold affecting their life. So far, all has been good with battery life. Each of the lighting strips comes with its own USB-C to USB-A type lead. The adjustment capabilities include... OFF Moon Symbol - will only activate light in the lowest of lights when movement detected Sun Symbol - will activate light regardless of ambient light, when movement is detected ON - the light is on all of the time, regardless of light or movements detection. A Big Light symbol - 5 levels of brightens to use. The fifth being exceptionally bright, the first being quite dim. A temperature / thermometer symbol - The light temperate, from warm light to stark white light. Three settings. The lighting strips are easy to remove to charge, and yet secure enough to not have fallen off from their fittings. I do recommend using their included card template, the help in the correct placement of the magnetic adhesive strips, once fitted try and not peel off to adjust. These are very much recommended, just be aware that they are NOT rated for outdoor use, that will also include areas like a bathroom, if it has high humidity.
